and besieged it.
And when he was unable to subdue it,
he sent and summoned his brother al-Kamil.
And al-Kamil came and waged a fierce battle against Damascus,
and took it at the beginning of the eighth month,
and handed it over to al-Ashraf.
And al-Ashraf gave in exchange for Damascus to his brother al-Kamil: Edessa, Harran, Callinicus (Raqqa), Sarug, Ras 'Ayn, Muwazzar, and Jamlin (Jumlin?),
and he left to al-Nasir son of al-Mu'azzam, the lord of Damascus, the fortress of Karak, and Balqa, and the territory of Jerusalem, and Samaria.
And al-Kamil sent armies with al-Malik al-Muzaffar Taqi al-Din against Hama,
in order to take it from his brother, al-Malik al-Nasir Qilij Arslan.
Now the latter came down secretly from the fortress and went to al-Kamil,
and promised him gold,
so that he would not expel him from Hama.
But al-Kamil would not accept.
Then al-Nasir said to al-Kamil:
"If by all means you take Hama from me,
then swear to me that you will take it for yourself,
and will not give it to my brother Taqi al-Din."
And al-Kamil swore,
and sent his men to take delivery of the city.
The people of the city, however, and of the fortress refused and said:
"Apart from our king,
no one shall rule over us."
And they began to fight vigorously.
Then al-Kamil sent to them:
"Behold, your king Taqi al-Din is with you;
surrender to him."
And the citizens rejoiced with great joy,
and surrendered to Taqi al-Din,
and he entered and went up to the fortress.
And after some days he went to Harran to al-Kamil, who had gone to inspect the territories that had been given to him.
And he honored him greatly and loved him,
and gave him his daughter as a wife.
And he clothed him,
and all who were with him,
and sent him again to Hama.
For slanderers had said to him:
"Taqi al-Din will never again come down from the fortress of Hama,
and you will not see him."
And when he went openly,
he honored him greatly.
And in that same year Sultan 'Ala al-Din gained control over the cities of Erzincan and Kamacha (Kemah).
